ShortDescription.Value: Drivers route around traffic jams the way a navigation app with live traffic would: fewer queues, far fewer jam warnings, no measurable slowdown.

Publish.LongDescription:
**Live Traffic Routing** makes drivers react to the traffic that is on the roads **right now**.
In the base game, drivers only learn very slowly (over game days) which roads are *usually* busy, and once they set off they never change their mind. With this mod, a road that is jammed right now looks slow to the route planner, so new trips pick another way, and drivers already on the road switch to a faster route when the way ahead jams up. Like a navigation app with live traffic.
**What it does** - Live traffic: measures how fast cars actually drive on every lane, every few game minutes, and feeds it into the game's own route planner. - Re-routing while driving: cars, delivery trucks (including semi-trailers) and taxis re-plan mid-trip when their route gets much slower, using the game's own re-routing. Buses and other public transport keep to their lines. - Simple presets: Relaxed, Balanced (recommended) and Eager. Picking one fills in the sliders; tweak any slider for your own mix. - New in 1.1: drivers also look at where everyone else is about to drive, so traffic spreads over several detours instead of all piling onto one, and local streets that suddenly get much more traffic than usual look slower to drivers passing through. - New in 1.1: ambulances, fire engines and police cars on an emergency run re-route around jams too. Drivers re-route at the next junction where there is a real choice. - New in 1.1: an **Auto** preset that tunes itself to your city, one small tested step at a time. - New in 1.1: **Temporary roadworks** (in the statistics panel): close a road for traffic, or ask drivers to avoid or prefer it, to test your network without deleting anything. These marks are temporary: they are not saved and are cleared when you load a save. - New in 1.1: a **bottleneck finder** (statistics panel, Causes tab): where each queue actually starts and why (traffic lights, turning across oncoming traffic, give way, lanes merging, people crossing, buses or service vehicles stopping in the lane, and more), shown on the map with the lanes and turns of the junction, where the stuck drivers come from and go to, and what you can do about it: lane and turn advice, and new roads or missing turns that would let the drivers skip the queue. It ranks problems over the last 24 game hours and tells you when a fix worked.
**Tested results (one 100k city, Balanced vs the mod off, same save, same game hours; your city will differ with its road network)** - About 28% fewer vehicles waiting in queues - About 87% fewer jam warnings on the map - Real driving speed up about 3% - Only slightly more traffic on local streets (about 10%) - No measurable slowdown at the fastest game speed: the mod itself uses about 1% of one CPU core and about 5 MB of memory (tested in a 100k city)
Eager pushes harder (queues down about 38%) but sends noticeably more traffic through neighbourhoods. Relaxed is a light touch.
These results were measured with version 1.0. The 1.1 additions start from first estimates and are still being tested; the presets may change with the results.
**For traffic geeks (optional, off by default)** Turn on **Statistics panel** in the options to get a traffic icon in the game with a Live Traffic panel: how traffic is doing right now, the busiest streets and junctions (click one to jump there), charts per hour of the day, why the cars in queues are on the road, the mod's cost, and side-by-side comparisons between the mod off and different settings, with a check of whether a difference is real or just the simulation's randomness. Every game hour is saved to ModsData/LiveTrafficRouting/captures.csv for your own spreadsheets. You choose how long statistics are kept (1 game month to unlimited), and while recording, milestone popups don't pause your test. With the panel off, nothing is recorded.
**Feedback welcome** Especially from big cities (250k+) and players using other traffic mods. Please report bugs and share results at https://github.com/Yhanli/LiveTrafficRouting/issues. If traffic looks off, turn on **Statistics panel** and **Write traffic report to log**, and attach a screenshot of the Compare or Cost tab and Logs/LiveTrafficRouting.log: that shows exactly what the mod did in your city.
**Good to know** - Nothing is stored in your save. You can turn the mod off (Options) or remove it at any time; the game's own traffic behaviour comes straight back. - The mod replaces the game's traffic flow system (the traffic flow info view works as before). Other mods that also replace it may not work together with this one. - Emergency vehicles on an emergency run are re-routed mid-trip; other service vehicles (garbage, post, hearses, maintenance) are not. - Live traffic can only help where another route exists. If every route ends in the same queue (one highway exit, one entrance to a cargo yard), drivers have nowhere to go: build a second connection. The Hotspots tab in the statistics panel shows where the queues are. - Settings texts are in English.
Publish.ChangeLog: 1.1.0: Traffic forecast ("Spread drivers over detours": roads many drivers are heading for look busier before they jam), "Keep through traffic out of neighbourhoods", emergency vehicles re-route, re-routes (also in a standing jam) wait for a junction with a real choice and never start inside a junction, the re-route limit follows how busy the route planner is, a self-tuning Auto preset, temporary roadworks (close, avoid or prefer a road; not saved). Statistics panel: bottleneck finder (Causes tab: where queues start and why, with a map view of lanes, turns and where drivers come from and go to, lane and junction advice, new road and turn ideas that let drivers skip the queue, a 24-hour ranking that shows when a fix worked), how people travel (car share, walking, cycling, public transport, waiting for a route), vehicles the game removes when stuck and where, traffic news, Copy summary. Fixes: local streets are now recognised correctly (the game stores speed limits at about twice the shown value), cyclists are no longer counted as car passengers, the previous session's log is kept. The new settings start from first estimates and are still being tested. 1.0.0: First release: live traffic routing, re-routing while driving for cars, delivery trucks and taxis, presets (Relaxed, Balanced, Eager), and an optional statistics panel for traffic geeks.
